core_claim: Cognition is grounded in sensorimotor experience; understanding and thought involve simulating action and perception. Environmental affordances activate motor schemas and simulated action; space is understood through bodily possibility and potential movement.

seminal_works.title: The brain's concepts: The role of the sensory-motor system in conceptual knowledge
seminal_works.full_citation: Gallese, V., & Lakoff, G. (2005). The brain's concepts: The role of the sensory-motor system in conceptual knowledge. Cognitive Neurodynamics, 1(1), 2-96.

falsification_criteria: Observing actions does not activate motor cortex/cerebellum; no motor simulation occurs
Disrupting motor preparation (TMS, lesion) does not impair action understanding or language comprehension
Enacting an action (physically performing it) does not improve memory or understanding compared to passive observation
scope_boundaries: Applies well to action understanding, basic semantic concepts, and skill learning
Does NOT fully explain abstract concepts (justice, democracy, mathematics) or amodal reasoning
Scope LIMITED to animals with motor systems; less clear for plants or non-motile organisms

environmental_predictions.statement: Environments that afford rich motor exploration (climbing, reaching, balancing, grasping opportunities) activate broader motor simulations and support more flexible, embodied understanding of spatial concepts
environmental_predictions.mechanism: Affordance activation engages premotor/motor cortex. Rich sensorimotor experience builds detailed body schema and motor-semantic mappings (e.g., 'tall' is mapped to upward reaching action).

competing_predictions.prediction: Action understanding depends on direct affordance perception, not motor simulation

environmental_predictions.statement: Constrained environments (limited movement, no reaching/climbing) narrow motor preparation and impair flexible reasoning about spatial/action concepts; abstract cognition becomes more detached from bodily grounding
environmental_predictions.mechanism: Motor simulation requires motor preparation. Constraints prevent action exploration → narrow sensorimotor corpus → less flexible embodied semantics → more amodal (abstract) reasoning.

environmental_predictions.statement: Architectural spaces that match human body scale (doors proportional to height, stairs to leg length, reaching distances) activate optimal motor schemas; mismatches require conscious compensation and reduce efficiency
environmental_predictions.mechanism: Body-scaled affordances activate pre-tuned motor schemas automatically. Non-scaled spaces require effortful motor recalibration and conscious attention to movement.

competing_predictions.prediction: Scaled environments reduce cognitive load, not because of motor matching, but because they look 'right' (affective fluency)

characteristic_questions: What action possibilities does this environment afford (reaching, grasping, climbing, balancing)?
What body-scaled relationships exist (door heights, stair proportions, work surface heights)?
Does the environment permit or constrain motor exploration and enactment?
What motor resonance (imitation potential, action observation) is triggered by environmental features?
How does the spatial layout activate forward models of movement (body path simulation)?

panel_persona.voice: I think about cognition through the body and movement. What affordances activate motor schemas? How does physical embodiment ground spatial understanding and action concepts?
typical_critiques: Mirror neuron evidence is controversial (some studies show null effects); don't overstate the mechanism.
Embodiment is real, but human language and abstract thought transcend sensorimotor grounding.
Behavioral enactment effects are robust, but alternative explanations exist (elaboration, attention, distinctiveness).
Not all motor simulation is conscious; distinguish automatic resonance from deliberate mental simulation.
blind_spots: May underestimate how thoroughly humans can reason abstractly and symbolically (amodal cognition is possible)
Overestimates the breadth of motor simulation; most cognition is not grounded in action
Limited account of how language permits decoupling from embodiment (metaphor, imagination, fiction)
Does not explain why some people are more embodied reasoners than others (personality, experience, training)
complementary_frameworks: predictive-processing (forward models in motor simulation serve prediction error minimization)
spatial-navigation (body-relative spatial representations (egocentric) scaffolding allocentric maps)
ecological-dynamics (affordances are the link between motor schemas and environmental structure)
neuromodulatory-systems (dopamine motivation shapes which affordances are motorically simulated vs. ignored)

meta.notes: Mirror neuron discovery was groundbreaking; subsequent controversy about scope (not every action understanding requires simulation). Embodied cognition is influential but not monolithic. Body-scaling in architecture largely understudied empirically.
